registered.content: An async-generator core with a thin, transport-agnostic flush layer automatically solves back-pressure, reconnection, and type safety while letting the same code run over SSE or WebSocket without rewrites.

The streaming layer is tightly coupled to VS-Code’s extension host and fails the moment you need real back-pressure, proxy compatibility, or memory predictability; a simple fetch + ReadableStream achieves lower latency and zero-config portability without the WebSocket/SSE complexity.
The streaming code is a minimal pipe, not a production-grade layer; keep the zero-config spirit but add a 1–2 kB client-side buffer and a fallback to raw fetch to survive outside VS-Code.

registered.content: One generator returning raw OpenAI chunks plus a thin re-yield wrapper gives us observability, zero-copy streaming, and a client schema in <50 lines—something cline-cline currently spreads over five files and 300+ lines.

Agno’s streaming abstraction adds more moving parts than it removes; the existing SSE loop is already the thinnest possible layer, and any ‘auditability’ gain is offset by the new coupling to Agno’s internal event taxonomy.
Lift the 60-line generator pattern, not the whole framework; it slots into our current SSE endpoint with zero breakage and gives us a clean place to stream partial deltas.
